items.title: Iran agrees to surrender enriched uranium as US deal nears, officials say

items.description: President Donald Trump announced Saturday that a peace agreement with Iran has been "largely negotiated," including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global energy waterway that has been closed during the conflict between the two nations.

items.title: Ebola patients flee DRC facility after arson as cases near 800

featured_image.name: Ebola Patients Flee After Second Treatment Tent Set on Fire—'Panic'

items.description: The Ebola outbreak tearing through eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has grown to nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths, with the disease now spreading across borders into Uganda and prompting emergency declarations from global health authorities.

items.title: Russia fires Oreshnik missile in massive assault on Kyiv

featured_image.name: Russia launched Oreshnik missile at Kyiv Oblast in overnight attack ...

items.description:
Russia unleashed one of its most devastating aerial assaults on Kyiv since the full-scale invasion began, firing 90 missiles and 600 drones at the Ukrainian capital and surrounding areas overnight Sunday, killing at least four people and wounding more than 80, according to Ukrainian officials.[1][2]

Multiple rounds of explosions were heard across the city throughout the early morning hours in a bombardment that lasted more than five hours, damaging residential buildings, schools, markets, and a trade center across the capital.[3][4]

items.title: Zelensky calls Germany's associate EU membership plan 'unfair'

featured_image.name: Exclusive-Ukraine's Zelenskiy says proposal of associate EU ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told EU leaders in a letter sent late on Friday that a German proposal to grant Ukraine "associate" membership of the European Union was "unfair" because it would leave Kyiv without a voice inside the bloc, according to Reuters, which reviewed the message.[1][2]

"It would be unfair for Ukraine to be present in the European Union, but remain voiceless," Zelensky wrote. "The time is right to move forward with Ukraine's membership in a full and meaningful way."[2][1]

items.title: Taiwan says China deployed 100-plus vessels after Trump-Xi summit

featured_image.name: Chinese military exercises foreshadow a blockade of Taiwan

items.description: Taiwan's National Security Council chief Joseph Wu said Saturday that China has deployed more than 100 navy, coast guard, and other vessels across regional waters in what marks one of Beijing's largest maritime shows of force in recent memory, raising alarm over China's intentions toward the self-governing island.[1][2][3]

items.title: U.S. has 'almost completely excluded' Israel from Iran talks, officials say

featured_image.name: US has almost completely excluded Israel from negotiations with ...

items.description: The United States has "almost completely excluded" Israel from ongoing negotiations with Iran, Israeli defense officials told The New York Times this week, as a widening rift between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu threatens to reshape Middle Eastern geopolitics.[1]

items.title: Zelensky confirms strike on chemical plant 1,700 km inside Russia

featured_image.name: Ukrainian drones strike Russian chemical giant's plant over 1,700  kilometers from front lines

items.description: Ukraine escalated its long-range drone campaign overnight on May 23, hitting an oil terminal in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk and a chemical plant nearly 1,700 kilometers from the border, as Kyiv continues to target the energy and industrial infrastructure underpinning Russia's war machine.

items.title: Ukraine hits Russian frigate, oil terminals in Novorossiysk

featured_image.name: Frigate Admiral Essen of the Black Sea Fleet of the Russian Federation in  Sevastopol Bay

items.description: Ukrainian forces launched a multi-target overnight assault on the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk on the night of May 22-23, hitting the frigate Admiral Essen, a missile hovercraft, and oil infrastructure, according to Ukrainian military sources and Russian officials.

items.title: US naval blockade of Iran hits 100 redirected ships

featured_image.name: CENTCOM boasts month-long Iran naval blockade, redirecting 67 commercial  ships

items.description:
U.S. Central Command announced on Friday that American forces have redirected more than 100 commercial vessels since the naval blockade of Iranian ports began on April 13, marking a milestone in the six-week-old maritime operation designed to choke off Tehran's oil exports.[1][2]

The achievement comes as CENTCOM steadily escalated its enforcement figures — from 37 ships redirected by April 25, to 58 by May 8, 67 by May 12, 85 by May 18, and 94 as of May 21 — underscoring the pace of commercial traffic still attempting to reach Iranian waters despite the blockade.[3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: Rubio invites Modi to White House amid trade impasse

featured_image.name: Marco Rubio holds talks with PM Modi during Delhi…

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Saturday, extending a White House invitation on behalf of President Donald Trump as Washington seeks to stabilize a relationship frayed by trade disputes and competing geopolitical pressures.[1][2]

Rubio's four-day visit — his first official trip to India — comes as the two countries navigate a complicated trade landscape shaped by court rulings that dismantled much of Trump's tariff architecture and new investigations that could reimpose duties on Indian goods.

items.title: NATO weighs return to Iraq after wartime evacuation

featured_image.name: NATO Relocates Iraq Mission Staff to Europe Citing Security Concerns -  Bloomberg

items.description:
NATO's advisory mission to Iraq, which was fully evacuated to southern Italy amid the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, could return to Baghdad in the coming months, the mission's former commander said this week.

French General Christophe Hintzy, who handed command of NATO Mission Iraq to Spanish General Ramon Armada during a change-of-command ceremony this week, told AFP that "the general staff is working on various options" to allow the mission to resume operations inside Iraq.[1][2]

items.title: SpaceX launches first Starship V3 but loses booster over Gulf of Mexico

featured_image.name: SpaceX's upgraded Starship V3 blasts off in debut test flight from Texas |  Reuters

items.description:
SpaceX launched its upgraded Starship V3 megarocket on Friday evening from Starbase, Texas, marking the debut of the company's most powerful rocket design yet. While the upper stage successfully deployed 22 dummy Starlink satellites and completed a controlled splashdown in the Indian Ocean, the Super Heavy booster crashed uncontrolled into the Gulf of Mexico after its engines failed to perform as planned.

The flight, which lifted off at 5:33 p.m. CDT from SpaceX's new Pad 2, came one day after a hydraulic pin on the launch tower arm failed to retract, scrubbing the first attempt at T-minus 40 seconds. Upper-level winds pushed the launch from its initial 5:30 p.m. window to 6:30 p.m. CDT on Friday.[1][2]

items.title: 4 dead, 90 trapped in China coal mine after CO buildup

featured_image.name: Chinese coal miners killed by carbon monoxide poisoning

items.description: Four workers have been confirmed dead and 90 remain trapped underground after carbon monoxide levels exceeded safe limits at a coal mine in Changzhi City, in northern China's Shanxi Province, according to a Reuters report citing the state news agency Xinhua.[1][2]

items.title: Iran condemns US sanctions on its envoy to Lebanon

featured_image.name: Sheibani, an Iranian Diplomat with Intelligence Clout

items.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Friday strongly condemned the US Treasury Department's decision to sanction Tehran's designated ambassador to Lebanon, Mohammad Reza Sheibani, calling the move "illegal and unjustified" and accusing Washington of violating international law and the UN Charter.[1][2][3]

items.title: WHO upgrades Congo Ebola risk to 'very high' as cases surge

featured_image.name: ?url=http%3A%2F%2Fnpr-brightspot.s3.amazonaws.com%2F40%2F50%2F29437dd2447cb7ae2b417ee2125d%2Fap26140529940548.jpg

items.description:
The World Health Organization on Friday upgraded its risk assessment for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo from "high" to "very high" at the national level, as the rapidly escalating epidemic now encompasses nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.[1]

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the outbreak is "spreading rapidly" and warned that the actual scale is likely far larger than official figures suggest. There are now 82 confirmed cases in the DRC along with seven confirmed fatalities, but Tedros indicated the true toll could exceed 1,000 infections, with cases significantly underreported for months before detection.[2][1]

items.title: Rubio cites 'slight progress' in US-Iran peace talks

featured_image.name: Marco Rubio says U.S. expects Iran response on peace deal 'today'

items.description:
Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in Tehran as Islamabad pushed to narrow the remaining gaps between Washington and Tehran in stalled peace negotiations. Speaking at a NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg, Sweden, Secretary of State Marco Rubio offered a cautious assessment of the diplomatic efforts.

"There has been some slight progress. I don't want to exaggerate it, but there's been a little bit of movement, and that's good," Rubio told reporters on Friday.[1][2][3]

items.title: NATO allies bewildered by Trump's troop reversal

featured_image.name: Trump pledges an additional 5,000 troops for Poland in apparent u-turn

items.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Helsingborg, Sweden, on Friday for a NATO foreign ministers' meeting, carrying a message from President Donald Trump about allied shortcomings during the Iran conflict while trying to calm growing European anxiety over Washington's shifting military commitments on the continent.

items.title: Palestinian envoy drops UN vice presidency bid after US threats

featured_image.name: Trump administration pressures Palestinian UN envoy to drop General  Assembly vice presidency bid | Reuters

items.description: Palestinian Ambassador Riyad Mansour has withdrawn his candidacy for a vice president position at the UN General Assembly following pressure from the Trump administration, the United Nations confirmed on Thursday. Lebanon's ambassador will assume the role in his place.[1][2]

items.title: Russia developing seabed nuclear missiles, German investigation finds

featured_image.name: Russia slates drills for nuclear forces

items.description:
NATO intelligence services have been closely tracking Russia's Northern Fleet amid growing concerns that Moscow is advancing a secret program to deploy nuclear-armed missiles on the Arctic Ocean seabed, according to an investigation published on May 21 by German public broadcasters WDR and NDR. The report identifies a classified project codenamed "Skif," under which Russia is believed to be developing remote-controlled missile systems housed in sealed containers dropped from submarines to the ocean floor.[1][2][3]

The revelation comes as Russia wraps up its largest nuclear exercises in years, a three-day drill running from May 19 through May 21 that mobilized nearly 65,000 troops, over 200 missile launchers, 140 aircraft, 73 surface vessels, and 13 submarines — including eight strategic nuclear submarines.[4][5]

items.title: Trump, Rubio reject Iran's plan for Hormuz toll system

featured_image.name: Trump says US opposes Strait of Hormuz tolls, vows to get uranium from Iran

items.description: Iran is in active talks with Oman to establish a permanent toll system for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, formalizing Tehran's control over one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints. The move drew sharp rebukes from both President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Thursday.
